operator_visible_outcome: Source-policy implementation and tests are split by cohesive policy ownership without changing accepted repositories, diagnostics or command outcomes

inputs.validation: Bounded tracked source-policy implementation, test, fixture, build-target and analyser-configuration inventories

outputs.validation: Deterministic source-policy acceptance or rejection with the existing bounded diagnostic and exit status

canonical_state: Command dispatch, manifest policy, file scanning, bounded source reading, tracked inventory and Rust syntax are owned by main.go, manifest.go, scan.go, source.go, inventory.go and rustsyntax.go
Go skip detection, target-matrix selection, package loading and CGO policy are owned by goskip.go, gotarget.go, goload.go and gocgo.go
Go AST inspection, TestMain policy and process-exit detection are owned by goinspect.go, gotestmain.go and goexit.go
Source suppressions, golangci configuration, Cargo manifest policy and Cargo execution overrides are owned by suppression.go, golangci.go, cargo.go and cargoconfig.go
Runner tests remain in main_test.go while every other test and fault fixture follows its named production owner
The architecture checker remains a separate cohesive source-policy file and is not folded into command dispatch
derived_state: Focused command, manifest, inventory, bounded-read, Go target, loader, CGO, exit, Rust, Cargo, suppression and independent Assurance verdicts

authorities.grant: Accept only the exact declared source-policy split files while preserving bounded fail-closed policy behaviour
authorities.refusal: Reject a mixed-responsibility file, missing destination, undeclared sibling, duplicated declaration, unbounded read, skipped target or changed policy outcome

authorities.grant: Independently compare the exact source-policy inventory and known-bad policy outcomes
authorities.refusal: Reject changed ownership, bounds, inventory, target, exit, suppression or configuration semantics

trust_boundaries.treatment: Parse only bounded tracked inputs and compare exact source, declaration, test and fixture ownership with this manifest
Challenge Product acceptance using independent inventory, target-matrix and known-bad policy fixtures
Parse bounded canonical output, preserve failure distinctions and reject missing, malformed, truncated or contradictory results

resources.acquisition: Read one bounded NUL-delimited tracked-file inventory
resources.bound: At most 100000 paths, 16777216 aggregate source bytes and 30000 milliseconds
resources.release: Release inventory and parsed syntax when policy evaluation returns
resources.cleanup_failure: Return an infrastructure error without accepting the tree

resources.acquisition: Open only an inventory-selected source, manifest or analyser configuration
resources.bound: At most the existing per-file and aggregate byte limits with bounded diagnostics
resources.release: Close the file and release decoded syntax before returning
resources.cleanup_failure: Return a policy failure without accepting partial evidence

resources.acquisition: Start only an existing enumerated Go or Cargo inspection command
resources.bound: One bounded command invocation per declared control with inherited cancellation
resources.release: Wait for the process and retain its bounded outcome before returning
resources.cleanup_failure: Return an infrastructure error without converting failure to acceptance

resources.acquisition: Read one bounded strict architecture policy document and its declared fixtures
resources.bound: At most 1048576 bytes per inventory or fixture
resources.release: Release decoded policy when independent evaluation returns
resources.cleanup_failure: Return an assurance error without accepting the tree

platforms.evidence: Native Production and Assurance policy execution

invariants.statement: Every source-policy declaration, test, fixture and command remains owned by exactly one declared cohesive destination
invariants.boundary: Tracked source-policy file to declared responsibility
invariants.falsifier: A declaration, test or fixture is missing, duplicated, left in a mixed-responsibility file or moved beneath the wrong owner

production_controls.owner: exact source-policy file, declaration, test and fixture inventory

assurance_controls.owner: independent source-policy ownership and inventory comparison

invariants.residual_uncertainty: Structural ownership does not itself prove policy semantic equivalence

invariants.statement: Tracked inventory, manifest, source and analyser-configuration parsing remains bounded and fails closed
invariants.boundary: Untrusted repository or tool bytes to policy decision
invariants.falsifier: An oversized, truncated, malformed, non-canonical, untracked or unreadable input yields acceptance or an unbounded diagnostic

production_controls.owner: bounded source, inventory, manifest and parser fixtures

assurance_controls.owner: independent malformed, oversized, truncation and inventory fixtures

invariants.residual_uncertainty: The configured bounds limit inspected material and cannot establish absence outside the governed tracked inventory

invariants.statement: Go skip, target-matrix, package-load, CGO, TestMain and process-exit policy outcomes remain unchanged
invariants.boundary: Go source and tool output to governed test and build inventory
invariants.falsifier: A governed target or test is skipped, a forbidden CGO or process-exit path passes or tool failure is treated as absence

production_controls.owner: Go skip, target, loader, CGO, TestMain and exit-policy fixtures

assurance_controls.owner: independent build-constraint, inventory and exit-status challenges

invariants.residual_uncertainty: Cross-target static analysis does not constitute native platform execution

invariants.statement: Rust syntax, Cargo manifests, Cargo execution overrides and source-suppression policy remain fail closed and semantically unchanged
invariants.boundary: Rust, Cargo and analyser configuration to repository policy verdict
invariants.falsifier: A hidden target, execution override, conditional suppression, malformed attribute or analyser exclusion passes policy

production_controls.owner: Rust syntax, Cargo and suppression policy fixtures

assurance_controls.owner: independent Rust, Cargo and suppression known-bad fixtures

invariants.residual_uncertainty: Textual configuration inspection proves only the maintained declared forms

success_semantics: Accepted means the exact declared source-policy split preserves command results, bounded parsing, governed inventories, target selection, process-exit distinctions and analyser controls
refusal_semantics: A mixed owner, missing destination, undeclared sibling, changed inventory, unbounded input, skipped governed target or policy bypass returns a bounded rejection
failure_semantics: Malformed policy, read or parse failure, unavailable required tooling, abnormal tool exit or incomplete evidence fails the gate
cancellation_semantics: Cancellation stops owned inspection work and cannot produce acceptance
indeterminate_semantics: Missing, contradictory, truncated or unavailable required evidence cannot produce acceptance
recovery_semantics: Rerun from the unchanged tracked inventory; no partial source-policy result is canonical or retained
compatibility_or_reset_policy: Unused pre-release source is split directly; the original mixed files are deleted and no wrapper, forwarding file, duplicate implementation or compatibility surface is retained
falsifiers: A declaration, test, fixture or exact command changes ownership during the split
An original mixed-responsibility file remains or a declared destination is missing
An undeclared sibling source or test file appears beneath tools/sourcepolicy
An oversized, malformed, truncated, non-canonical or unreadable input produces acceptance
A governed Go target, package, test, CGO case or process-exit path escapes inspection
A Rust attribute, Cargo target, execution override, suppression or analyser exclusion escapes policy
A tool failure, cancellation or incomplete inventory is converted into absence or acceptance
The architecture checker is folded into command dispatch or Product becomes dependent on Assurance

production_controls.owner: exact source-policy file, declaration, test and fixture inventory
bounded source, inventory, manifest and parser fixtures
Go skip, target, loader, CGO, TestMain and exit-policy fixtures
Rust syntax, Cargo and suppression policy fixtures

assurance_controls.owner: independent source-policy ownership and inventory comparison
independent malformed, oversized, truncation and inventory fixtures
independent build-constraint, inventory and exit-status challenges
independent Rust, Cargo and suppression known-bad fixtures

residual_limitations: This structural split does not establish new repository policy
The source-policy tool remains Product code and cannot provide its own independent verdict
Native Windows execution remains separately governed
Exact-pair sign-off requires committed clean Product and Assurance candidates
non_goals: Change any accepted or rejected repository state, diagnostic or exit status
Add a source language, analyser, suppression form, build target or policy rule
Create an interface, wrapper, registry, option or duplicate implementation
Fold the architecture checker into command dispatch
Delete, weaken or replace a known-bad fixture
Change operation, protocol, persistence, supervision, worker or platform behaviour
deletion_criteria: Delete this slice contract only when a later reviewed contract explicitly supersedes the source-policy split inventory
